prompt:
Edit the FIRST image, the red-haired archer. Repaint ONLY the illumination, shadow and reflection design across her existing surfaces. Preserve her face identity, crimson high ponytail silhouette, rich violet/gold costume, exposed shoulders/arms/thighs, all garment and armor shapes, pose, anatomy, bow and arrow, framing and transparent cutout. The SECOND image is a reference for restrained, coherent illustrated lighting and connected material planes; do not copy its character, palette, text, chibi or backdrop.

The current archer's lighting is unsuccessful: almost every pale skin patch and ivory lining has the same brightness, while shoulder, bracer, knee and shoe contain disconnected gold glints and brown reflective patches. Remove that existing patchwork lighting and paint a deliberate whole-character lighting design.

Use broad, soft, art-directed diffuse illumination with a clear focal hierarchy. No cinematic spotlight, rim-light halo or dramatic dark vignette. The principal lit region is her face, nearby front hair mass, top-facing shoulder armor and the upper plane of the outstretched arm. Let light follow connected volumes instead of independently illuminating each costume component. Keep the face warm and fully readable without bleaching it.

Build a coherent family of deeper, slightly cooler local-color shadows beneath the chin, along the side of the chest, under the upper arm and along the side of the waist. Carry compatible shadow color into the rear ponytail, interiors of overlapping skirt panels, folded rear leg and underside of the forward leg. Exposed thighs remain warm skin but read as quieter middle values than the face, not two equally bright flesh-colored spotlights. The ivory skirt lining also belongs to its actual turned-away shadow plane, instead of reading as luminous white. This is deliberate form modeling, NOT a uniform top-to-bottom dark gradient.

For hair, retain its existing shapes and rich crimson color, but replace repetitive shiny stripes and small angular light patches with broad connected light and shadow regions spanning neighboring locks. The front crown and nearby bangs receive the main light; rear hair is quieter and connected. Give the curved masses a modest soft transition, not many isolated facets.

For every gold armor plate first restore a continuous warm gold middle-tone surface. Model its curvature with one broad connected turning shadow and a restrained broad reflected-light change. Remove mottled brown islands, white triangles, jagged mirror reflections and gold speckles. Preserve only true seams, relief and engraved ornament. Keep a few thin controlled highlights near the focal shoulder upper edge and bow-holding bracer. The knee guard, shoe and lower bow receive NO sharp white glare and NO uninterrupted bright perimeter outline; their material reads through thickness, coherent large planes and subdued local transitions. Keep gold clearly gold, not gray or flat yellow plastic.

For violet cloth, keep the saturated violet local color intact. Remove the patchwork of small light/dark polygons; show form through continuous fabric planes and only existing necessary structural folds. A stable local color must remain visible through changes in illumination. Use clear selective edges at real occlusions and limited soft transitions across round forms, borrowing the second reference's economy. Do not airbrush away all structural boundaries and do not add paper texture, scratches or noise.

Maintain the requested lively crimson, violet and warm gold colors. Reduce competing LOCAL highlights, not overall saturation or global exposure. Shadows still contain distinct local colors; do not turn the lower body black, muddy, transparent or indistinct. Keep the clean complete silhouette and all existing character details. Do not add ornaments, change hairstyle, change costume or increase/decrease exposure.

Deliver ONE image with actual transparent alpha, including all gaps. No haze, colored background, cast floor shadow, glow, scenery, decorative border, text or checkerboard pixels. Ignore the latent background RGB in the inputs' transparent regions.
